item.text:
**4B.9 Research Note**
Overall read: **mostly negative**. The strongest 2024 evidence is for broad digital controls, social-media monitoring, and administrative harassment of critics, with only narrow, reactive crisis-response behavior on the positive side.

- [Indonesia: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/indonesia/freedom-net/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | Kominfo retained direct content-restriction power without appeals, and an election-period task force involving Bawaslu, KPU, Kominfo, and police cyber units was used to target “hoax” and polarizing content. This is strong evidence for state digital control over political speech. | `4B.9`, `4B.6`, `4B.5`
- [Indonesia: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/indonesia/freedom-net/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | Critics, journalists, and internet users faced criminal prosecution, violent attacks, harassment, and self-censorship pressure; disinformation also proliferated ahead of the election. This is direct negative evidence for administrative harassment and digital pressure. | `4B.9`, `4B.6`, `4B.7`
- [Indonesia: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/indonesia/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | The press environment remained constrained, journalists faced arrest/harassment/violence, and activism in Papua and on corruption remained risky; the report also notes bureaucratic obstacles and deportation risk for foreign journalists in Papua. This supports a negative reading on political freedom under digital and administrative pressure. | `4B.9`, `4B.6`, `4B.7`
- [2025 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Indonesia](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128570.html) | U.S. Department of State | 2025-08-12; covers 2024 | The report says police temporarily detained critics and peaceful demonstrators, especially in Papua, and that the government did not systematically investigate abuses. That is negative evidence for administrative harassment and coercive political control. | `4B.9`, `4B.7`, `4B.4`
- [Protests across Indonesia as parliament delays change to election law](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/protests-across-indonesia-as-parliament-delays-change-to-election-law-3582501) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-22 | Reuters reported that security forces used tear gas and water cannon during the election-law crisis. This is not digital control, but it is direct evidence of coercive administrative suppression of political mobilization. | `4B.9`, `4B.5`, `4B.7`
- [Jokowi orders audit of Indonesia's data centres after cyberattack](https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/southeast-asia/article/3268495/jokowi-orders-audit-indonesias-data-centres-after-cyberattack) | Reuters via South China Morning Post | 2024-06-28 | After a major ransomware attack, Jokowi ordered an audit of government data centres. This is a narrow, remedial response rather than repression, so it is weak positive evidence against a blanket “surveillance state” reading. | `4B.9`
- [President Jokowi asks quick mitigation over alleged NPWP leak](https://www.antaranews.com/berita/4345027/presiden-jokowi-minta-perlunya-mitigasi-soal-kebocoran-data-npwp) | ANTARA News | 2024-09-19 | Jokowi ordered Kominfo, Finance, and BSSN to mitigate the alleged taxpayer-data breach quickly. This is another limited crisis-management response, but it does not show protection of political freedom by itself. | `4B.9`

**Search gap**
- I found **no credible evidence of a nationwide internet shutdown ordered by Jokowi in 2024**.
- I also did not find strong primary-source evidence of a documented, large-scale spyware campaign in 2024.
- The clearest pattern is instead **localized connectivity restrictions, content takedowns, social-media monitoring, and harassment of critics**, especially around elections and in Papua.
